messages:
Alex Kim: Hey team — ran `terraform plan` against staging and it's showing ~1600 replacements after the provider refactor :grimacing:
Maya Patel: Ugh. Can you paste the top of the plan or the provider diff?
Alex Kim: Snippet:
```
# aws_instance.web will be replaced
-/+ provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws"]
+/+ provider["registry.terraform.io/custom/aws-client"]
```
Alex Kim: Looks like the provider address changed for most aws resources; state still points to the old provider namespace.
Jon Erickson: Did you run `terraform init -upgrade`? sometimes init will remove old provider cache but won't rewrite state addresses.
Alex Kim: Yep, init -upgrade done. Plan still wants to recreate. State list shows addresses referencing the old provider.
Priya Rao: We probably need `terraform state replace-provider` to remap addresses. Example:
```
terraform state replace-provider \
  'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws' \
  'registry.terraform.io/custom/aws-client'
```
Maya Patel: Run that in a non-prod workspace first and snapshot state (S3 backup). That command is irreversible if you do it wrong.
infra-bot: CI: staging plan failed — blocking deploys (lock acquired by ci-runner-42)
Jon Erickson: Also check if any modules are still declaring `provider = aws.some_alias` — provider aliases can make the replacement tricky.
Alex Kim: Good call — module A uses `alias = "client"` and module B doesn't. Could cause mixed provider addresses.
Priya Rao: If aliases differ you may need to run `terraform state mv` for specific resources after replace-provider. Eg:
```
terraform state mv 'module.foo.aws_instance.bar' 'module.foo.aws_instance.bar'
```
(not very pretty but helps remap)
Maya Patel: I'll give Alex a hand. Alex — can you create a state backup and share S3 key, then tag me on the PR with the replace-provider command and a plan output?
Alex Kim: Backed up (s3://tf-state-backups/staging/backup-2034567850.tfstate), creating a branch now. I'll run replace-provider in a temp workspace and push the plan.
Jon Erickson: Heads-up: do it during low-traffic window — we'll coordinate with oncall. Also add a rollback note if things go sideways.
Priya Rao: If you prefer, we can do this with `terraform state pull` -> local replace of provider strings -> `terraform state push` in a controlled window.
Maya Patel: Prefer `replace-provider` since it preserves meta-info. But both fine if we document steps.
Alex Kim: Plan from the test run looks clean after replace-provider + init -upgrade. Pushing a PR with steps and `tf plan` output.
infra-bot: Note: remember to release the state lock after manual ops: `aws s3 rm s3://tf-state-locks/staging/lockfile` if the lock is stale :warning:
Maya Patel: Thanks. I'll review the PR and run it with you tomorrow 9:30am PST.
Jon Erickson: I'll page oncall when you start.
Alex Kim: Thanks all — will tag when ready :thumbsup:
